summary: The only source change appends .catch to the cached base-tip promise in fallbackTip; it is behavior-neutral because fallback already awaits that promise inside its own try/catch, so a thrown readRef and a resolved failed both yield null inputs with unchanged read counts and metrics. The remaining additions are fake-port regression tests over fallback behavior the base already implements.

evidence: Base src/repair/loop-live-inputs.ts already defines LIVE_INPUT_FALLBACK_CONCURRENCY = 4 plus primeFallback and the shared fallbackTips cache; the candidate source diff only appends .catch to that cached promise.
fallback awaits fallbackTip inside its own try/catch (lines 240-242), so the new catch changes no inputs, read counts or metrics: both paths produce null inputs.

Base tests/repair/loop-input-gate_test.ts already covers this behavior: unavailable batches bound fallback latency across a hot tier (74 records, peak concurrency 4, one shared readRef per repository) and concurrent fallbacks share failed base-tip observations, including a throwing readRef.
The added tests at lines 492-667 restate the same bounded fallback for 60 records and do not introduce a throughput reduction beyond the base commit.
